ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Bird-Call Recognition Across Distance: Acoustic Degradation and BirdNET Performance
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.26757v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As bird calls weaken with distance, their recordings lose spectral detail. We examine how species recognition varies with distance using controlled playback of ten-second excerpts from 20 bird species at seven distances from 1 to 48 ft. An STM32-based recording system acquires and stores the audio, which is subsequently analyzed on a computer using acoustic measurements and BirdNET. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Efficient Conversational Multi-Talker ASR with Predicted Speaker-Agnostic Activity Streams
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.26796v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-talker automatic speech recognition (ASR) can be performed by conditioning a single-speaker recognizer on frame-level speaker activity. However, this approach requires a complete diarization pass to obtain the conditioning signals and one ASR pass per speaker, making both the frontend and recognition costs dependent on the number of speakers. We reduce these costs by using Heuristic Error Assignment Training (HEAT) to merge the activities of an arbitrary number of speakers into two speaker-agnostic streams. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Emotion-Aware Prefix: Towards Explicit Emotion Control in Voice Conversion Models
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2603.09120v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent advances in zero-shot voice conversion have exhibited potential in emotion control, yet the performance is suboptimal or inconsistent due to their limited expressive capacity. We propose Emotion-Aware Prefix for explicit emotion control in a two-stage voice conversion backbone. We significantly improve emotion conversion performance, doubling the baseline Emotion Conversion Accuracy (ECA) from 42.40% to 85.50% while maintaining linguistic integrity and speech quality, without compromising speaker identity. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2605.16681v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Audio super-resolution (SR), also referred to as bandwidth extension (BWE), aims to reconstruct high-fidelity signals from low-resolution (LR) or band-limited (BL) observations, an inherently ill-posed task due to the ambiguity of missing high-frequency (HF) content. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the field, with a particular focus on the paradigm shift from discriminative mapping to modern generative modeling. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Asymmetric Phase Coding Audio Watermarking
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2605.07241v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The proliferation of deepfake audio challenges voice-based authentication, and passive forensic detectors are sensitive to evolving generative models and to real-world channel distortions. We propose Asymmetric Phase Coding (APC), a training-free cryptographic signing layer for audio that anyone holding the public key can verify offline, designed as a compact and auditable provenance primitive that can stand alone or be stacked with learned watermarks. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.26831v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio tagging is a fundamental task in machine listening, enabling the automatic identification of acoustic events in applications such as intelligent monitoring, industrial inspection, environmental sensing, and smart environments. As these applications increasingly migrate to edge platforms, deployment-oriented metrics such as latency, energy consumption, and resource utilization become critical alongside predictive performance. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: A Novel Dataset and Framework for Schenkerian Optical Music Recognition
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.26958v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Music theory enables performers, composers, and listeners to engage more deeply with music. Schenkerian analysis (SchA) is a particularly illustrative and widely used approach for modeling tonal structure, organizing music into hierarchical layers of harmonic and voice-leading relationships. Despite its importance in pedagogy and scholarship, producing well-formatted Schenkerian graphs remains difficult. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: EAF-TTS: Rethinking Codec-Latent Coordinates for Flow TTS
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.27214v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Latent text-to-speech (TTS) systems generate codec latents decoded by a frozen decoder, but good reconstruction does not ensure geometry suitable for Flow generation from isotropic Gaussian noise. We present Embedded Acoustic Flow TTS (EAF-TTS), an acoustic-latent adaptation of ELF with phone- and duration-conditioned generation, shared-network terminal correction, and frozen WaveVAE decoding. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Neural Defend Ranks #1 in Global Audio Deepfake Detection Benchmark - ARCAS on the Podonos Independent Leaderboard
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.27215v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Commercial detectors of AI-generated audio are usually promoted with results on internal test sets that buyers cannot inspect. Independent benchmarks with private labels give a more reliable comparison. We report the results of Neural Defend's ARCAS foundation models on the Podonos audio deepfake detection benchmark, an independent leaderboard that scores commercial detection APIs and open-source detectors on one held-out set of real speech and speech from current text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems, delivered in six file formats, against l

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.27601v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spoken dialogue synthesis aims to generate multi-turn conversational speech from dialogue scripts while maintaining speaker consistency and contextual appropriateness. However, existing models largely lack fine-grained controllability, which is critical for capturing the dynamic, context-dependent style shifts in natural conversations. While prompt-based TTS has enabled such control for single-speaker speech, existing datasets heavily rely on predefined tags, which fundamentally limits their capacity to capture open-ended styles. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.27784v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice cloning now needs only seconds of audio, and detectors tuned to one dataset often fail when the generator, channel, or language changes. We introduce ARCAS 290M, Neural Defend's foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. A single frozen production model, with no benchmark-specific fine-tuning, generalizes across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Windchime: an Audiovisual Installation with Audio-Language Model implementations
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.26759v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Windchime is an audiovisual installation in which spoken language retrieves music and interactive animations from an artist authored corpus. A local Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model transcribes each prompt while an audio-language model (ALM) embeds it and retrieval over 406 audio stems returns a soundscape with live coded Strudel fragments that layer into audio output. Simultaneously each spoken input results in retrieval of interactive Three.js animation scenes each containing unique tactile control via monome grid and arc hardware. W

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.27810v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Audio language models (ALMs) can answer clinical questions from speech, outperforming baselines built on handcrafted acoustic features. Reasoning ALMs generate a chain of thought that refers to properties of the speaker's voice before predicting. Each statement the model makes about the voice needs to be checked against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. On clinical speech, existing evaluations score only the final answer. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Rhythm-TTS: High-Fidelity Shortcut Latent Modeling and Probabilistic Rhythm Generation for Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2510.02848v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) systems are commonly built on either discrete codec tokens or continuous acoustic representations. Discrete-token models benefit from stable sequence modeling and explicit speech factorization, but they ultimately synthesize speech through codebook lookup and codeword composition, which can accumulate errors and impose a quality ceiling on naturalness and speaker similarity. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: The Voice on the Line
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.35272v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: A transcriber listening through one microphone also hears everyone near it. We train causal voice isolators that keep only the caller for a speech recogniser: masking transformers with 20 ms of latency that enroll the caller from the call itself. Short evaluation windows hide two failures that real calls expose: forgetting the caller when another voice talks alone for a while, and damaging a caller who is alone. The underground resists, nerd style, and it's all happening thanks to the Fediverse and the fantastic Brighton-based Gravitons.

CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Berlin Kraftwerk, the former power plant in Berlin Mitte associated with Tresor and Ohm, was the venue last week for Helsing's launch of new agentic technology, Clarity. This platform uses the same controversial AI-driven approach implicated in accelerating the use of flawed intelligence and killing civilians in Palestine, Lebanon, and Iran. Kraftwerk's Head of Sales has taken sole responsibility and apologized. But the fiasco seems emblematic of Berlin's pivot from cultural capital to military-industrial capital, with the money that follows.

CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
The masterful artist Ryo Fujimoto works in electronics not just as a passive actor behind machines, but fully embodied in physicality, voice, and sometimes screams. He sends his latest live performance -- an arresting, but ultimately healing performance that takes on war and violence in a powerful machine-vocal cry.
